solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Source of cutting gear and machinery

definitions.meaning: a gardener's cutting is a shoot taken from a growing specimen, its source
industrial equipment and machinery collectively are called ..., as in heavy ...

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the cutting equipment and machines came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting is a slip taken from a growing specimen, while factory equipment is known collectively by the same word.

clue.text: Part of training regime on ship has youngsters boxing

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the youngsters go around the other pieces

parts.note: pups are young animals, youngsters
re means on or about, as in a memo
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A regime on board ship includes the young crew boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport, but it signals enclosing. RE is the crossword convention for 'on', meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: An exercise routine commonly includes lowering and raising the body on the arms from the floor.

clue.text: Main channel's receiver concealing coating of rust

definitions.note: an arterial is a main road or route, used here as a noun

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the receiver holds the rust letters

parts.note: an aerial is an antenna that receives signals

indicators.note: a coating is on the outside, so only the outer letters of rust are taken

explanation.surface: A TV station's antenna is covered in a layer of rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main channel' sounds like television but means a major route; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Main roads and big blood vessels carrying flow from the heart are described with this word, and the road can be a noun.

clue.text: Gain worth cryptically having a fit

indicators.note: cryptically tells the solver to read the answer itself as a piece of crossword wordplay

parts.note: the first two words of the answer, jumbled with the last word as the anagram signal, spell these letters

explanation.surface: Getting value in a puzzling way while losing your temper.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: treat the answer as wordplay, with 'wobbly' as an anagram signal acting on THROWINGA, and you get GAIN WORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing your temper in a sudden tantrum is a British idiom for having a fit.

clue.text: On paper, maintain shortcut

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper, here the paper the puzzle itself appears in
to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand by a shortcut in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcut is a device or route that saves minutes and hours, a labour-saving measure.

clue.text: Last few batsmen lie, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a tale is a falsehood, a lie

explanation.surface: Rumours circulate about the lower-order batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the weakest batsmen come in at the end of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the lower-order batsmen at the end of the innings are collectively called by this word, like the end of an animal.

clue.text: Engineer chappie on island turned up dead

parts.note: a chappie is a man, a chap

indicators.note: turned means the word up is read backwards

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: An engineer living on an island has turned up dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' is a verb here: to contrive or rig something.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome is to contrive it by skilful handling, often deviously.

clue.text: Arguments from rivals after quiet jaunt

indicators.note: after means the rivals word comes after the jaunt pieces

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
an outing is a jaunt or trip
matches can mean equals or rivals, as in 'more than a match for'

explanation.surface: Rivals fall out after a quiet day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud quarrels in which both sides raise their voices are heated arguments.

clue.text: Tacky individual originally in very small plainclothes unit

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word individual

parts.note: the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police's plainclothes detective branch

explanation.surface: A tacky person joins a tiny undercover police squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacky' means sticky, not tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something viscid is thick and sticky, which is the literal sense of tacky like wet paint.

clue.text: Coarse stuff from contrary girl booked after game?

indicators.note: after means the girl's name follows the game letters

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union

indicators.note: contrary means turned the opposite way, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is a girl in a book, Hardy's novel

explanation.surface: A wayward girl is cautioned after a match, using rough language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' looks like a referee's caution but marks the girl as one from a book: Hardy's Tess.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet was a coarse reddish-brown homespun cloth once worn by country folk.

clue.text: Blackmail English team hosting wrong side at Lord's

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside, so the team word holds the wrong word within it

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team
a tort is a civil wrong in law
in cricket the on side is the leg side of the field; Lord's is London's famous cricket ground

explanation.surface: An England cricket team is pressured into letting the wrong side play at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' signals the container. In cricket the on side, also called the leg side, is one half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is obtaining money by threats, which is the essence of extortion.

clue.text: Unseats judge avoiding historic conflicts

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so the judge's letter is left out

parts.note: jousts were medieval combats between mounted knights

explanation.surface: A judge sidesteps old battles while removing people from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes the J from JOUSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat a rider or official is to remove or expel them from their place.

clue.text: Records describing campaign returned to lounge

indicators.note: returned means the whole assembled string is read backwards
to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the records go around the campaign

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
a war is a military campaign

explanation.surface: Records that tell of a military campaign are brought back to a lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing a line round, so it signals a container; 'returned' then reverses the whole of LWARPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to stretch out lazily, the same as to spread oneself out sprawling on a sofa.

clue.text: Traditional requirements for roasting shrew?

parts.note: a joint used to be roasted on a skewer over flames, and those two words together make a word for a hot-tempered woman

explanation.surface: A recipe query about what you need to cook a small rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into SPIT and FIRE, the old way of roasting meat; 'shrew' is not the animal but a bad-tempered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew in the old sense is a scolding, fiery-tempered woman, exactly what the answer describes.

clue.text: Composer's lightest note in rising melody

parts.note: palest means lightest in colour

indicators.note: in puts the note letter inside the reversed melody
in a down answer rising means reading upwards, so the melody word is reversed

parts.note: an air is a melody or tune

explanation.surface: A composer's softest note sits in a climbing tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses AIR to RIA, and 'in' places N inside it; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was the great Italian Renaissance composer of sacred music.

clue.text: Not too good east of prairies for a picnic

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so the poorly word comes after the grassland word

parts.note: prairies are great grassy plains
someone ailing is unwell, not feeling too good

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell somewhere east of the American prairies, on the way to a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is 'a picnic' is easy, and smooth easy progress is the idiom used here.

clue.text: Artist with tight clothing threatening swimmer

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover all round, so the tight word wraps the artist

parts.note: stingy means tight with money
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter in close-fitting clothes is a menacing swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray with a venomous barbed tail is a dangerous fish of the sea.

clue.text: China, third-rate location for alpines

parts.note: C is a third-rate grade, after A and B
alpine plants are often grown in a garden rock bed

explanation.surface: China is dismissed as third-rate, unlike the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is the dishware, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cups and other dishes made of porcelain are called china, the earthenware a household uses.

clue.text: Overact badly, receiving worried member's standard warning

indicators.note: the shuffled letters receive the other pieces inside them
doing something badly scrambles it, so the letters of overact are rearranged

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A worried MP gets the usual warning not to overdo things on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns the clue's first word into CAVETOR, and 'receiving' puts the two inner pieces inside it, after its fourth letter. ATE for 'worried' is the 'what's eating you?' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase 'let the buyer beware' is the standard caution given to purchasers.

clue.text: Conclude sappers like working

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, RE, are the army's sappers
as means like
on means working, switched on

explanation.surface: Army engineers decide they like being on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason something out is to conclude or infer it by logical thought.

clue.text: Lash out, taking extremely lucrative journey

indicators.note: extremely points to the two extreme letters, first and last, of lucrative

parts.note: a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone spends wildly while on a profitable trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To act or spend without restraint is to let go wildly, an idiom for lashing out.

clue.text: Last of shade still protecting excessively hot canine

indicators.note: last of tells us to take only the final letter of the word shade
a protector surrounds what it shields, so the still word goes round the excessively word

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'still to come'
too means excessively, as in 'too much'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A dog keeps out of the heat in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' makes YETOOT, a container. 'Canine' looks like a dog but is the pointed tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is the long pointed tooth below the eye, and the upper ones are popularly called by this name.

clue.text: Niche product ultimately diverted folk

indicators.note: diverted means sent a different way, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word product

explanation.surface: A niche product, in the end, is redirected to a folk market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges NICHE plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk as an adjective, in folk dance or folk costume, describes traditional cultural groups, matching the adjective for a people's culture.

clue.text: Brass section's top piercing note

indicators.note: piercing means passing into, so that letter goes inside the note

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: top means the first letter of section, the top of a down entry

explanation.surface: In an orchestra, the brass section's top player hits a shrill note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' is British slang for money, not the instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass and the answer are both informal British slang words for money.

clue.text: Cultivated bush sheltering rook perhaps?

indicators.note: to shelter is to hold safe inside, so the rook letter goes within
cultivated soil is worked over, so the letters of bush are turned over

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A garden bush that might house a nesting rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' rearranges BUSH to SHUB, and 'sheltering' takes R inside. Read whole, the clue also describes a garden plant that a bird might nest in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultivated bush in a garden is a woody plant, which may well give shelter to a bird such as a rook.

clue.text: Eg Clydesdale press first to show revolutionary engine

indicators.note: first means the press word comes before the Clydesdale word

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a Clydesdale is a breed of heavy Scottish draught horse

explanation.surface: Pressing the image of a Clydesdale to show off a revolutionary engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' refers to the wheels going round and the change railways brought.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam locomotive was nicknamed for replacing draught animals, so a railway engine earned that name.

clue.text: Knock over empty potty; headstrong toddler may get it

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the knock word is read backwards

parts.note: to pan or knock something is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters, so potty loses its middle

parts.note: rash means headstrong or reckless

explanation.surface: A wilful toddler tips over an empty potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses PAN to NAP, and 'empty' reduces POTTY to PY.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies and toddlers in damp nappies (diapers) often get a skin irritation on the bottom.

clue.text: Try case of larceny hesitantly

parts.note: to have a shy at something is to have a go or try, as at a coconut shy

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so only the first and last letters of larceny are kept

explanation.surface: A suspect is hesitantly tried on a theft charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a bashful, timid way means going about it hesitantly.
